title: Root-Zone Water Content as a Spatial and Temporal State

content.overview: Root-zone water content is not one uniform number. It varies with media physical properties, container geometry, root distribution, irrigation pattern, evaporation and transpiration, so representative placement and repeated measurement matter.

vocabulary.definition: Water volume expressed relative to the volume of the measured root-zone material.
How a substrate stores and releases water under the specific container, compaction and root conditions.
Meaningful difference in moisture or chemistry across positions within one container, slab or zone.

sections.title: Media and geometry shape the measurement
sections.body: Soilless media differ in porosity, water retention and aeration, and those properties can shift with particle size, compaction and container geometry. Report the system context with water-content data.

sections.title: Sensor placement defines the question
sections.body: A single probe can miss dry or wet regions elsewhere in the root zone. Verify placement and compare representative positions when spatial disagreement is plausible.

sections.title: Crop demand changes the trajectory
sections.body: Plant size, root establishment, light, VPD and irrigation distribution influence how quickly water content changes between events.

workedExamples: Two containers receive the same volume but show different water-content profiles because one has a different substrate packing and root distribution.
commonMistakes: Treating one sensor as the whole root zone.
Comparing values across different media without context.
Assuming equal applied volume creates equal stored water.
content.practicalApplication: Map three root-zone positions before and after irrigation and describe where the measurements agree, disagree and what that means for representativeness.
content.summary: Root-zone water content is a measured distribution and trajectory, not a universal single target.
